blocks.en: Learning Goal

blocks.en: After studying this unit you will be able to use the Question Method from Unit 8 of WiseSpeak to plan a complete evangelistic sermon. You will select a plural noun keyword from the text, form a clear subject, build three short parallel points (each five words or less), and write a one-sentence evangelistic objective that leads listeners to Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Después de estudiar esta unidad podrá usar el Método de la Pregunta de la Unidad 8 de WiseSpeak para planificar un sermón evangelístico completo. Seleccionará una palabra clave (sustantivo plural) del texto, formará un tema claro, construirá tres puntos cortos y paralelos (cada uno de cinco palabras o menos) y escribirá un objetivo evangelístico de una sola oración que lleve a los oyentes a Cristo.

blocks.en: The Question Method in WiseSpeak
blocks.es_reference: El Método de la Pregunta en WiseSpeak

blocks.en: In Unit 8 of WiseSpeak we learned four practical planning methods for evangelistic sermons. The Question Method is one of the most powerful because it begins with the very question the text itself is answering. We read the passage, identify the central question it raises or answers, and let that question guide the entire sermon.
blocks.es_reference: En la Unidad 8 de WiseSpeak aprendimos cuatro métodos prácticos de planificación para sermones evangelísticos. El Método de la Pregunta es uno de los más poderosos porque comienza con la misma pregunta que el texto mismo está respondiendo. Leemos el pasaje, identificamos la pregunta central que plantea o responde y dejamos que esa pregunta guíe todo el sermón.

blocks.en: The Inductive Approach
blocks.es_reference: El Enfoque Inductivo

blocks.en: The Question Method follows the inductive approach taught in the first seven units of WiseSpeak. We start with the specific facts in the text and work backward to discover the keyword and subject. The Question Method keeps the sermon focused and personal. It forces the preacher to speak directly to the listener's real need. When combined with the keyword approach, the result is a clear, unified evangelistic message that calls for a definite response.
blocks.es_reference: El Método de la Pregunta sigue el enfoque inductivo enseñado en las primeras siete unidades de WiseSpeak. Comenzamos con los hechos específicos del texto y trabajamos hacia atrás para descubrir la palabra clave y el tema. El Método de la Pregunta mantiene el sermón enfocado y personal. Obliga al predicador a hablar directamente a la necesidad real del oyente. Cuando se combina con el enfoque de la palabra clave, el resultado es un mensaje evangelístico claro y unificado que llama a una respuesta definida.

blocks.en: How the Question Method Works
blocks.es_reference: Cómo Funciona el Método de la Pregunta

blocks.en: Read the chosen text carefully.
blocks.es_reference: Leer el texto elegido con cuidado.

blocks.en: Ask the probing question the text answers.
blocks.es_reference: Hacer la pregunta de sondeo que el texto responde.

blocks.en: Turn the main idea into a plural noun keyword.
blocks.es_reference: Convertir la idea principal en una palabra clave (sustantivo plural).

blocks.en: Form the subject around the keyword.
blocks.es_reference: Formar el tema alrededor de la palabra clave.

blocks.en: List the specific answers or truths in the text. Turn each truth into a short point (five words or less) that is a singular of the keyword.
blocks.es_reference: Listar las respuestas o verdades específicas del texto. Convertir cada verdad en un punto corto (cinco palabras o menos) que sea un singular de la palabra clave.

blocks.en: Write a one-sentence evangelistic objective.
blocks.es_reference: Escribir un objetivo evangelístico de una sola oración.

blocks.en: Add a clear invitation at the end.
blocks.es_reference: Agregar una invitación clara al final.

blocks.en: The keyword is always a plural noun. Every point is a clean singular of that plural keyword. The points stay short and parallel so the listener can remember them easily. When a single verse does not contain every point needed, we add supporting texts from other passages while the keyword still holds the whole sermon together.
blocks.es_reference: La palabra clave es siempre un sustantivo plural. Cada punto es un singular limpio de esa palabra clave plural. Los puntos se mantienen cortos y paralelos para que el oyente pueda recordarlos fácilmente. Cuando un solo versículo no contiene cada punto necesario, agregamos textos de apoyo de otros pasajes mientras la palabra clave mantiene unido todo el sermón.

blocks.en: Example from Acts 16 — The Philippian Jailer
blocks.es_reference: Ejemplo de Hechos 16 — El Carcelero de Filipos

blocks.en: The text asks the question, "What must I do to be saved?" The keyword is "steps" (a plural noun). The subject is "Three Steps to Salvation."
blocks.es_reference: El texto pregunta: "¿Qué debo hacer para ser salvo?" La palabra clave es "pasos" (un sustantivo plural). El tema es "Tres Pasos para la Salvación".

blocks.en: Question: What must I do to be saved? · Keyword: steps
blocks.es_reference: Pregunta: ¿Qué debo hacer para ser salvo? · Palabra clave: pasos

blocks.en: Hear the gospel.
blocks.es_reference: Escuchar el evangelio.

blocks.en: Believe in Jesus.
blocks.es_reference: Creer en Jesús.

blocks.en: Be baptized.
blocks.es_reference: Ser bautizado.

blocks.en: Each point is a singular of the keyword "steps." Each point is five words or less. The points are parallel. The sermon begins with the specific facts in the text and works backward to form the keyword and subject. This is pure inductive preaching as taught in WiseSpeak.
blocks.es_reference: Cada punto es un singular de la palabra clave "pasos". Cada punto tiene cinco palabras o menos. Los puntos son paralelos. El sermón comienza con los hechos específicos del texto y trabaja hacia atrás para formar la palabra clave y el tema. Esto es pura predicación inductiva tal como se enseña en WiseSpeak.

blocks.en: Example from John 3:16
blocks.es_reference: Ejemplo de Juan 3:16

blocks.en: The text answers the question, "Why did God send His Son?" The keyword is "reasons" (a plural noun). The subject is "Three Reasons God Sent His Son."
blocks.es_reference: El texto responde a la pregunta: "¿Por qué envió Dios a Su Hijo?" La palabra clave es "razones" (un sustantivo plural). El tema es "Tres Razones por las que Dios Envió a Su Hijo".

blocks.en: Question: Why did God send His Son? · Keyword: reasons
blocks.es_reference: Pregunta: ¿Por qué envió Dios a Su Hijo? · Palabra clave: razones

blocks.en: Show His love.
blocks.es_reference: Mostrar Su amor.

blocks.en: Offer eternal life.
blocks.es_reference: Ofrecer vida eterna.

blocks.en: Save the world.
blocks.es_reference: Salvar al mundo.

blocks.en: Each point is a singular of the keyword "reasons." Each point is short and parallel. The sermon stays anchored in the text.
blocks.es_reference: Cada punto es un singular de la palabra clave "razones". Cada punto es corto y paralelo. El sermón permanece anclado en el texto.

blocks.en: Example from Romans 10:9–10
blocks.es_reference: Ejemplo de Romanos 10:9–10

blocks.en: The text answers the question, "How can I be saved?" The keyword is "conditions" (a plural noun). The subject is "God's Conditions for Salvation."
blocks.es_reference: El texto responde a la pregunta: "¿Cómo puedo ser salvo?" La palabra clave es "condiciones" (un sustantivo plural). El tema es "Las Condiciones de Dios para la Salvación".

blocks.en: Question: How can I be saved? · Keyword: conditions
blocks.es_reference: Pregunta: ¿Cómo puedo ser salvo? · Palabra clave: condiciones

blocks.en: Confess with your mouth.
blocks.es_reference: Confesar con la boca.

blocks.en: Believe in your heart.
blocks.es_reference: Creer en el corazón.

blocks.en: Receive God's salvation.
blocks.es_reference: Recibir la salvación de Dios.

blocks.en: Again the points are clean singulars of the keyword "conditions." The sermon is inductive, biblical, and easy to follow.
blocks.es_reference: Nuevamente los puntos son singulares limpios de la palabra clave "condiciones". El sermón es inductivo, bíblico y fácil de seguir.

blocks.en: Why the Question Method Is Powerful for Evangelistic Preaching
blocks.es_reference: Por Qué el Método de la Pregunta Es Poderoso para la Predicación Evangelística

blocks.en: The Question Method makes the sermon personal. It speaks directly to the listener's need. It keeps the message focused on one clear question and one clear answer. When the keyword is a plural noun and the points are short parallel singulars, the listener can remember the sermon and take it home. The one-sentence objective keeps the entire message aimed at conversion. This method works especially well when the text raises a direct question that people today are still asking.
blocks.es_reference: El Método de la Pregunta hace el sermón personal. Habla directamente a la necesidad del oyente. Mantiene el mensaje enfocado en una pregunta clara y una respuesta clara. Cuando la palabra clave es un sustantivo plural y los puntos son singulares cortos y paralelos, el oyente puede recordar el sermón y llevarlo a casa. El objetivo de una sola oración mantiene todo el mensaje apuntado a la conversión. Este método funciona especialmente bien cuando el texto plantea una pregunta directa que la gente hoy todavía se hace.

blocks.en: The Question Method also works when a single verse does not contain every point. We simply add supporting texts while the keyword controls the outline. The sermon remains unified and the points stay short.
blocks.es_reference: El Método de la Pregunta también funciona cuando un solo versículo no contiene cada punto. Simplemente agregamos textos de apoyo mientras la palabra clave controla el bosquejo. El sermón permanece unificado y los puntos se mantienen cortos.

blocks.en: Practical Steps to Use the Question Method in Your Preaching
blocks.es_reference: Pasos Prácticos para Usar el Método de la Pregunta en Su Predicación

blocks.en: Choose a text that answers a real human question. Write the probing question in one clear sentence. Select the plural noun keyword that best captures the answers in the text. Form the subject by placing the keyword at the end. Build exactly three short parallel points, each five words or less. Write the evangelistic objective in one sentence. Prepare a clear invitation that calls for immediate response. This method, taken directly from Unit 8 of WiseSpeak and combined with the keyword rules from the first seven units, gives every sermon a strong evangelistic purpose.
blocks.es_reference: Elija un texto que responda a una pregunta humana real. Escriba la pregunta de sondeo en una oración clara. Seleccione la palabra clave (sustantivo plural) que mejor capture las respuestas en el texto. Forme el tema colocando la palabra clave al final. Construya exactamente tres puntos cortos y paralelos, cada uno de cinco palabras o menos. Escriba el objetivo evangelístico en una oración. Prepare una invitación clara que llame a una respuesta inmediata. Este método, tomado directamente de la Unidad 8 de WiseSpeak y combinado con las reglas de la palabra clave de las primeras siete unidades, da a cada sermón un fuerte propósito evangelístico.

sa.prompt: Define the Question Method in your own words.
sa.model: The Question Method begins with the very question the text is answering. We read the passage, identify its central question, and let that question guide the sermon - choosing a plural-noun keyword and building points inductively as personal answers to the listener's real need.

sa.prompt: List the seven steps for using the Question Method.
sa.model: The seven steps are: read the text, identify the central question, select the plural-noun keyword, form the subject, build the short parallel points, write the one-sentence objective, and close with the invitation.

sa.prompt: What question does the Acts 16 passage ask, and what keyword and three points result?
sa.model: The Acts 16 passage asks 'What must I do to be saved?' The keyword is 'steps,' and the three points are: hear the gospel, believe in Jesus, be baptized - each a singular of the keyword.

sa.prompt: What question does John 3:16 answer, and what keyword and three points result?
sa.model: John 3:16 answers 'Why did God send His Son?' The keyword is 'reasons,' and the three points are: show His love, offer eternal life, save the world.

sa.prompt: What question does Romans 10:9–10 answer, and what keyword and three points result?
sa.model: Romans 10:9-10 answers 'How can I be saved?' The keyword is 'conditions,' and the three points are: confess with your mouth, believe in your heart, receive God's salvation.

sa.prompt: Why is the Question Method described as inductive rather than deductive?
sa.model: The Question Method is inductive rather than deductive because it begins with the specific facts and question in the text and works backward to the keyword and subject, letting the text speak instead of importing an outside theme.

sa.prompt: Why does this unit say the Question Method is especially powerful for evangelistic preaching?
sa.model: The Question Method is especially powerful for evangelism because it is personal and focused: starting from a real question forces the preacher to speak directly to the listener's need, making the message memorable and pointed toward conversion.

sa.prompt: How are the three outline points required to relate to the keyword?
sa.model: The three points must each be a short singular of the plural keyword, five words or less, and parallel in form. That keeps the outline unified and easy to remember.

sa.prompt: How does the Question Method handle the case when a single verse doesn't contain every point needed?
sa.model: When one verse does not contain every point, the Question Method adds supporting texts, but the chosen keyword still controls the outline so the added passages remain unified under one plural-noun keyword.

sa.prompt: Identify the family of planning methods this unit draws on, and explain which one this unit focuses on and how it works.
sa.model: WiseSpeak Unit 8 gives four practical planning methods, and this unit focuses on the Question Method. It works inductively: begin with the question the text answers, choose the plural-noun keyword, and build short parallel points as singulars of it.
